mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as predictor of 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window, or correlation with 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In UNRATE > 4.0% periods, S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 40% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and residential sales (RSAFS) indicates a contraction in the housing sector that reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) yields Rank IC < 0.03 over any 12-month window, or negative return prediction holds in < 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%), the Federal Reserve tightens policy to combat inflation, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0% periods, S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 40% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past 6 months indicates strong labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS as predictor of 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window, or correlation with 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In INDPRO < 100 periods, S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and real GDP (GDPC1) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown that reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction term (INDPRO * GDPC1) yields Rank IC < 0.03 over any 12-month window, or negative return prediction holds in < 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During housing market slowdowns (HOUST < 1500 for two consecutive months), reduced consumer confidence in housing investment lowers overall spending and corporate revenue growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In HOUST < 1500 periods, S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 40% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03.
